Blocks.Text: ACLs establish a relationship between a synced record and a group that can view that record. You can use the endpoints and methods defined in this document to establish and manage ACLs throughout the integration lifecycle.

ACLs are a relationship between a atsEntityId and atsEntityAclId. The atsEntityId represents the entity which needs restricted visibility and the atsEntityAclId is the identifier of the list of users which will have access.
For broader context on how ACLs are defined across multiple endpoints, see Sync ACLs Overview.
The latest API version is 202604. Use this version in the LinkedIn-Version header for all API requests to access the most recent features and improvements.

Query Tunneling -- Requests require query tunneling if the request URL is larger than LinkedIn's maximum URL length. See Query Tunneling and Migration Guide - Updated API Request Maximum Length for more details.
Compliance with LinkedIn API Breaking Change Policy
Usage of the Client Credential Flow (2-legged OAuth) for authentication.
Usage of the Versioning request format for endpoints and methods that require it as defined in this document.

Please submit batch calls grouped with no more than 100 records at a time.
Do not assign more than 10 ACLs per user.
Update ACLs when users or records are added or updated to prevent visibility issues.
The following entity types support ACL definition.
